summary: Kanabec County, MN tower near Pomroy Lake: 95-ft Aermotor stairway tower dated 1963 by the Minnesota Forest Service; still standing, with decayed stair treads reported.

facts.design: 95-foot Aermotor stairway tower with square cab
facts.agency: Mn MFS (Minnesota Forest Service, now the DNR forestry division), per the Kanabec County survey

visit.trail_note: Visit account describes a muddy road leading to the tower and decayed stair treads; no visit rules or current owner found

events.note: County survey gives 1963 as the date for the 95-foot Mn MFS stairway tower near Pomroy Lake

evidence.quote: This tower stands near Pomroy Lake and is under the Moose

evidence.supports: tower is under the Moose Lake Forestry Station
evidence.quote: Lake Forestry Station. Aermotor tower. Square cab.

evidence.supports: owner Mn MFS, date 1963, height 95 ft, stairway type

evidence.quote: Minnesota Forest Service, now Minnesota Department of Natural Resources, Forestry Division

evidence.supports: township and lake named for John Pomroy, a pioneer lumberman

notes_for_editor: Only one build-date source (the Kanabec County survey). No staffing or fire history found. Access level omitted: no source describes public access or the current owner. The survey places the tower under the Moose Lake Forestry Station, which may mean restricted access; not verified. The visit account reports decayed stair treads, so the story advises against climbing. Height converted from 95 ft (28.96 m, shown as 29.0). The FFLA index shows no NHLR number for this tower. Photo already in photos_manifest, so none added. Fact-check 2026-10-09: story said 'worn stairs'; the source says decay, so the story now says decaying stair treads.
